channel.title: Updated · Science
channel.description: Physics, space, chemistry, materials and Earth science

item.title: Rivers and lakes worldwide lost water abruptly during the record heat of 2023 and 2024, a Science study finds
item.description: River flow fell about 5.7% and active lake and reservoir storage 9.5% below the 1991–2020 average in 2023–24, the sharpest joint drop in a 35-year record. (EurekAlert (AAAS), Phys.org (TU Wien), Nature World News)

item.title: Satellite radar shows Lagos and Alexandria sinking faster than sea-level projections assume, raising flood risk in 20 African coastal cities
item.description: A Science Advances study maps land motion under 20 African coastal cities and estimates more than 7 million people and about $180 billion in assets at flood risk by 2050. (BBC News, Eurasia Review (Virginia Tech release))

item.title: Millisecond-scale imaging of fragmented earthquake rupture by near-source fiber-optic sensing
item.description: A fibre-optic cable beside a California fault recorded a magnitude 2 earthquake breaking in two adjacent patches 42 milliseconds apart, not as one smooth circular rupture. (Sangwoo Han, YoungHee Kim, Jaewoo Kim et al. · Rice University; Seoul National University; University of Washington)

item.title: Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing
item.description: Two "lenses" acting on photon number focus a 500-photon microwave state for sensing and then map the signal back near vacuum, giving a 19 dB gain over the standard quantum limit. (Ziyue Hua, Chuanlong Ma, Yilong Zhou et al.)

item.title: Lower central dark matter densities in nearby galaxies than predicted by simulations
item.description: Dynamical models of 136 nearby galaxies find central regions with less dark matter than standard simulations predict, and the affected region grows with galaxy mass. (Yu Lei, Ling Zhu, Meng Yang et al.)

item.title: Peatlands drained since 1800 account for about 2.7% of human-caused warming, and the effect could nearly double by 2100
item.description: An MIT-led study in Nature estimates that draining about 15% of the world's peatlands has caused roughly 2.7% of human-driven warming, with emissions set to continue for centuries. (MIT News, Ars Technica)

item.title: MIT team reports signatures of paraparticles, a third kind of particle statistics, in a lattice of superconducting qubits
item.description: Using 16 superconducting qubits, MIT researchers built excitations that pass three tests for paraparticles, objects that follow neither the boson nor the fermion rulebook. (New Scientist, arXiv)

item.title: A US judge finds a second planned seabed-mining lease sale, off the Northern Mariana Islands, violated the Endangered Species Act
item.description: A federal judge ruled that the wildlife review behind a 16 December seabed-mining lease sale off the Northern Mariana Islands ignored the mining the leases could eventually allow. (BBC, Earthjustice)

item.title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
item.description: River flow and lake and reservoir storage fell together worldwide in 2023 and 2024, the largest drop since 1991, with South America responsible for about 70% of the lost streamflow. (Pedro L. B. Chaffe, Georgia Destouni, Francis H. S. Chiew et al.)

item.title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake
item.description: The magnitude 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake of 2025 appears to have started in a rough part of the fault, a kind of zone usually thought to stop giant ruptures, before breaking into a smoother one. (Haipeng Luo, Fengzhou Tan, Zhangfeng Ma et al.)

item.title: Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway
item.description: A plasma process melts cement ingredients and forms clinker in seconds instead of hours, using electricity in place of fossil-fuelled kilns. (Qi Zheng, Haiyan Mao, Chengyao Liang et al.)

item.title: Hera's first close-ups show DART left a stadium-sized crater and a tumbling asteroid surrounded by boulders
item.description: ESA's Hera spacecraft has returned the first close images of Dimorphos, showing that NASA's 2022 DART impact carved a crater nearly as wide as the asteroid and left it tumbling. (CNN, Ars Technica)

item.title: Niobium phosphide wires a few nanometres wide conduct better as they shrink, the opposite of copper
item.description: A Stanford-led study in Nature reports that ribbons of the semimetal niobium phosphide only 5 to 6 nanometres wide become less resistive as they narrow, unlike copper chip wiring. (Tech Xplore (Stanford University release), Nature)

item.title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage
item.description: Draining peatlands since 1800 accounts for about 2.7% of today's human-caused warming influence, and the effect could nearly double by 2100 even if no more peatland is drained. (Jevan B. Yu, Etienne Fluet-Chouinard, Susan E. Page et al. · Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Pacific Northwest National Laboratory; University of Leicester; UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology)

item.title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
item.description: Delft physicists coupled two minimal Kitaev chains in a nanowire and observed coherent oscillations of fermion parity, which they describe as the first coherent control of a Majorana qubit. (Francesco Zatelli, Bart Roovers, Nick van Loo et al. · Delft University of Technology)

item.title: China launches Shenzhou-24 with a Pakistani astronaut, the first foreigner to fly on a Chinese crewed mission
item.description: Shenzhou-24 carried two Chinese astronauts and Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to the Tiangong space station, the first time a foreign crew member has flown in China's crewed programme. (BBC News, Phys.org (Associated Press))

item.title: NOAA closes a hurricane season split by El Niño: one Atlantic hurricane, record activity in the eastern Pacific
item.description: NOAA's end-of-season summary counts 10 Atlantic named storms and a single hurricane, against 20 named storms and eight major hurricanes in the eastern Pacific, a contrast it attributes to a very strong El Niño. (Phys.org (NOAA release), iHeart)

item.title: Interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer for low-loss soft ultrasonic interfaces
item.description: A dry, stretchy rubber built entirely from bottlebrush-shaped polymers transmits ultrasound efficiently without any gel and kept a wearable imager working for about nine days. (Shu Wang, Runze Li, Zihan Tang et al. · MIT; Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology; University of Wisconsin at Madison; National University of Singapore; Nanyang Technological University)

item.title: Small and large earthquakes driven by inelastic deformation in weak fault zones
item.description: An earthquake-cycle model that lets the rock around a fault deform permanently reproduces both small and large earthquakes, and suggests that fault zones can be mechanically very weak. (Peng Zhai, Yihe Huang, Jean-Paul Ampuero · University of Michigan)

item.title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
item.description: Pretreating the electrode of a perovskite solar cell so its molecular contact layer bonds at several points gives 27.3% efficiency and 94% retention after 400 cycles between -40 and 85 °C. (Jiaxin Wu, Hongzhuo Wu, Zuhong Zhang et al.)

item.title: Euclid finds the most distant quasar yet, a 360-million-solar-mass black hole 630 million years after the Big Bang
item.description: Euclid astronomers confirmed a quasar at redshift 8.13, the first beyond 8, whose slowly feeding 360-million-solar-mass black hole strains models of how early black holes grew. (Euclid Consortium, University of Hamburg, Phys.org)

item.title: Webb's dust map of Cassiopeia A suggests the star's inner layers merged shortly before it exploded
item.description: Webb resolved the chemistry of individual dust clumps in the Cassiopeia A supernova remnant and found signs that burning shells inside the star mixed, possibly hours before the explosion. (NASA, Phys.org)

item.title: NASA asks industry to build a 20-kilowatt fission reactor for the Moon, to be ready for launch by 2030
item.description: NASA issued a request for proposals for Lunar Reactor-1, a 20-kilowatt fission system meant to be launch-ready by 2030 and to run on the Moon for at least five years. (NASA)

item.title: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release
item.description: Hollow capsules with a single hole use the calm they create inside a turbulent fluid to collect particles of one chosen size and release them on demand. (Matteo Sabato, Sarah Chong, Yaocheng Li et al. · University of Chicago; New York University)

item.title: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations
item.description: Chemists report a modular reaction that assembles benzene rings carrying six different groups, with the position of each one fixed in advance by the choice of starting materials. (Guillaume Mollaert, Hang-Fei Tu, Jacob R. King et al. · ICIQ)

item.title: COP31 ends without an overall agreement after the EU and island states reject a text that does not name fossil fuels
item.description: The UN climate summit in Antalya closed on Sunday with its main political text unadopted, the first such outcome since 2000, after a dispute over whether to mention fossil fuels. (Phys.org (AFP), Health Policy Watch)

item.title: Robot dives beside the Challenger Deep recover the deepest explosive volcanic deposits ever documented
item.description: Seven remotely operated dives on the Mariana Trench wall found rocks from explosive eruptions at more than 6,000 metres depth, in a zone where young volcanism is not expected. (Frontiers in Earth Science, Phys.org)

item.title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
item.description: Measurements from 21 research cruises and a global chemistry model put atmospheric organic nitrogen falling on the oceans at 12.8 million tonnes a year, about 27% of all nitrogen deposition. (Xu Yu, Yumin Li, Guitao Shi et al. · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; Southern University of Science and Technology; Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology; East China Normal University; Ocean University of China; South China University of Technology)

item.title: Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling
item.description: Chips smaller than a grain of rice sit inside test tubes and wirelessly report the temperature of a chemical reaction every half-second. (Sukwoo Lee, Evan A. Weingarten, Michael F. Reynolds et al. · Stanford University; Cornell University; Emory University; OWiC Technologies)

item.title: Resolving the black hole sphere of influence in a hyperluminous obscured quasar at redshift 4.6
item.description: Radio observations of gas swirling at the centre of the most luminous known obscured quasar give the first motion-based mass for a supermassive black hole beyond redshift 2. (Mai Liao, Roberto J. Assef, Chao-Wei Tsai et al.)

item.title: EPFL theory predicts the heating power fusion plasmas need to enter high-confinement mode
item.description: Physicists at EPFL's Swiss Plasma Center have a single theory for the power needed to push tokamak plasmas into high-confinement mode, and say ITER has margin while SPARC is close to its limit. (Phys.org (EPFL release), arXiv (De Lucca et al.))

item.title: Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids
item.description: In a defect-free superfluid of ultracold atoms, widening a narrow channel first lowers its resistance and then, as the channel turns from one- to two-dimensional, raises it again, with a resistance minimum in between. (Simon Wili, Meng-Zi Huang, Tommaso Bonaccorsi et al.)

item.title: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
item.description: A flat cloud of ultracold potassium atoms simulates a massive relativistic quantum field in two dimensions of space, showing a tunable mass gap and topological domain walls, a step toward lab tests of early-universe physics. (Yansheng Zhang, Feiyang Wang, Paul H. C. Wong et al.)

item.title: BepiColombo reaches Mercury after an eight-year voyage and prepares to become the second spacecraft ever to orbit it
item.description: The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission has arrived at Mercury after more than eight years and is set to fire its thrusters to enter orbit, with science operations due to begin in April. (The Guardian, BBC News)

item.title: The US sells its first deep-sea mining leases, off American Samoa, to a single bidder days after a court faulted the review
item.description: The Interior Department sold two seabed lease areas covering 31.5 million acres off American Samoa for the $6 million minimum, with one company bidding, three days after a judge found the wildlife review unlawful. (gCaptain, Yahoo News (AFP), Nature World News)

item.title: Physicists send a "practically unblockable" message through a brick wall by moving an elevator's counterweight and measuring its gravity
item.description: University of Queensland physicists encoded the word "gravity" in the position of a 1.8-tonne elevator counterweight and read it through a wall with a gravimeter, at one bit per minute. (University of Queensland via EurekAlert!, The Guardian)

item.title: Quantum position verification with remote untrusted devices
item.description: Using entangled photons and a loophole-free Bell test across a 195-metre network, NIST-led researchers certified that a remote party really sat in a target region, without trusting its hardware. (Gautam A. Kavuri, Yanbao Zhang, Abigail R. Gookin et al. · National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST))

item.title: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality
item.description: On a superconducting quantum processor, Google researchers used contextuality to win cooperative games and solve a structured problem at success rates no classical strategy can reach. (Google Quantum AI and CollaboratorsS. Kumar, E. Rosenberg, A. Grajales Dau et al. · Google Quantum AI)

item.title: Astronomers watch a Sun-like star spiral into a supergiant in Andromeda, with Webb confirming the merger
item.description: A star of about 0.7 solar masses merged with a supergiant seven times the Sun's mass in Andromeda after only seven orbits, and Webb observed the aftermath 47 days after the outburst peaked. (NASA, Phys.org)

item.title: Fiji declares a national disaster and Tonga a state of emergency as El Niño drought deepens
item.description: Fiji's cabinet declared a nationwide natural disaster and Tonga a 27-day state of emergency as El Niño-driven drought cuts water supplies, with effects expected to last until at least mid-2027. (Phys.org (AFP), RNZ, NZ Herald)
